newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN COTTON FIRMS, SHORTAGE OF READY STOCK.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN COTTON FIRMS, SHORTAGE OF READY STOCK.

text.p: Cotton prices turned firm on the local market, dealer said.
Mill buying however remained lower but shortage of ready stock amid dwindling supplies triggered speculative support.

In the spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees at 1,070/1,120 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while in the Gujarat segment, Kalyan cotton rose by 100/200 rupees at 14,400/15,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg), wagad cotton rose by 200 rupees at 13,500 rupees and Kala-ginned rose by 100 rupees at 12,600 rupees per candy.
"Supplies are lower and we are witnessing shortage of good quality cotton at the tail end of the season," one broker said.
Unsold stock of 1.0-1.5 million bales (170 kg each) is left across the country and offerings by the stockist remained at a low ebb.
"Physical demand for millers however remained slow today but rising prices may prompt millers to enter the market again ahead of new season," he said.
